If there are more than two dead heats, the stakes are proportioned accordingly.Dual ForecastThis is where bettors can place a wager on which drivers will finish first and second. An each way bet basically places two wagers: a driver to win and to finish above another position. If the driver wins, both bets get paid out. The same applies for team bets in this market.Stage WinnerThis is prevalent in NASCAR and IndyCar, which has more laps than Formula One. You can bet on which driver or team will be in the lead after 25 laps, 50 laps, 100 laps and so on. These are the stages.Matchups/Head-to-HeadSportsbooks will put two drivers or two teams against each other, allowing bettors to choose which one will place higher. For teams, the bet is usually on the highest-placed driver for that particular team. This is one of the more popular F1 betting strategies. For example, if a market was being offered on F1 to see if Ferrari or Mercedes placed higher, the highest-placing Ferrari driver determines the result, even if both Mercedes drivers finish ahead of the second Ferrari driver. This means that bettors must consider both driver and car in situations like this.Group WinnerThis is offered in NASCAR. Sportsbooks will put a handful of drivers in groups and ask which will be the winner of the group.Top Car Make DriverThis is also specific to NASCAR, where you can bet on whether the winning driver will be in a particular car manufacturer, like Ford or Chevy. These are determined during qualifying racing, which typically takes place the day before the race. You can also bet on markets offering odds for who will finish in the top 5 or top 10 in qualifying, though these aren't necessarily  available for every race. The results of qualifying will often shift the race odds.Motor sports futures bettingFormula 1 bettingIn most cases, F1 futures usually apply to the next race. However, you can bet on season-long futures for F1 championship betting. The Drivers Championship is straightforward as it will be given to the driver who accumulates the most points over the season. The Constructors Championship takes into account the points for both team drivers. Only the top 10 finishers in each race score points, and those points are tallied over the season. The winning driver can be part of a constructors championship, but that's not always the case.NASCAR BettingNASCAR has different portions of the season. You can bet on marquee races for NASCAR in the futures market, and you can also wager on winners for these particular series.IndyCarThe major marquee futures market for IndyCar is the Indianapolis 500. While you can't pick multiple drivers to win an event in a parlay, you can pick multiple drivers to finish in the top 5 or top 10. You can also pick teams to finish in the top 5 or top 10.How to bet on motor sports live during a raceSportsbooks do offer live odds for motor sports, though this is likely a more prominent feature for NASCAR and IndyCar as opposed to F1. Driver and team odds will shift based on where they are in the grand scheme of the race. NASCAR and IndyCar allow for more leeway since there are more laps, while F1 can sometimes shift quickly towards one driver or team.Tips and strategies for how to bet on motor sportsDriver form does matter when it comes to racing, but the biggest predictor of success is usually how each team can adjust to conditions. Races can take place in all kinds of weather and team strategy can make or break the day. There are some teams that struggle to adjust, and bettors should know which teams those are before placing wagers. Historical track success often takes a back seat to current form. For example, Max Verstappen won the Canadian Grand Prix three years in a row and was a contender after starting second behind George Russell in 2025. When this happens, there will be a safety car deployed, and all drivers must line up behind the safety car until the wreck is managed. There are different rules for each association and sometimes the race organizer makes a call in the moment, but usually, the race cannot end on a caution flag. If the wreck is too big to clear in a reasonable amount of time, the race will end despite the caution flag being signaled. Overtime doesn't really exist, but usually there will be at least one additional lap of racing should the fallout of the crash get removed in a timely manner and the safety car gets taken off the track.FAQCan you bet on motor sports?As long as you are of legal age in a state where sports betting is legitimate, you should be able to find a sportsbook which provides racing and motor sports odds.Who to bet on for the Indy 500?Because the Indy 500 typically takes place over Memorial Day weekend, you'll have to wait for a bit before placing wagers on who will win the signature event. title: Kewan Lacy out for season with injury: What's next for the Ole Miss star RB? - CBS Sports
description: Lacy's injury-riddled season has negatively impacted his NFL Draft stock, but is that enough to warrant a return
body:
Lacy's injury-riddled season has negatively impacted his NFL Draft stock, but is that enough to warrant a return to college football in 2027?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In an unsurprising turn, Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to injury. Lacy has been dinged up all season, and he's been limited in most of the games he's played.Lacy hasn't played since the Rebels' loss to Texas on Oct. 24, and he finishes with just 388 yards and five touchdowns in six games. Coming into the season, expectations were high for Lacy following a monster 2025 campaign, but his inability to remain healthy derailed him almost immediately.Last season, Lacy was a breakout star for the Rebels. He led the country with 306 attempts, and he made the most of those opportunities with 1,567 yards and 24 touchdowns. Lacy also made an impact in the passing game with 29 catches for 177 yards, and his explosiveness was apparent every game.Lacy's absence and ineffectiveness have led to a big drop for the Rebels' rushing attack -- slipping from 176.3 yards per game last year to 147.3 yards per game in 2026.
Looking ahead, Lacy will have a big decision to make in the offseason. He should be one of the top NFL Draft prospects at running back, but he has the talent to be the first running back off the board. Would one more college season, in which he gashes defense while fully healthy, help him fly up draft boards? Would that even be worth the risk?Lacy's big offseason decisionAs a true sophomore last year, Lacy wasn't able to enter the NFL Draft, but that might have been as high as his stock could be.Now? That stock has taken a massive tumble. In his latest three-round NFL mock draft for CBS Sports, Mike Renner projected Lacy as the No. 59 overall pick to the Minnesota Vikings. If Lacy feels like he could raise his draft stock -- while making something comparable to second-round money -- he might be open to staying in college.
In the wake of Lacy's injury, Renner noted that Lacy is "not even close to first-round" after his disastrous 2026 season. Plus, NFL teams have questions about Lacy's size (5-foot-11 and 205 pounds) and health.It's also fair to wonder whether NFL teams have once again cooled on first-round running backs more broadly. The last five drafts have only featured first-round running backs three times, and the last two classes were particularly bad.2026: Jeremiyah Love -- No. 4 overall2026: Jadarian Price -- No. 32 overall2025: Ashton Jeanty -- No. 6 overall2025: Omarion Hampton -- No. 22 overall2023: Bijan Robinson -- No. 8 overall2023: Jahmyr Gibbs -- No. 12 overallThe last four first-round running backs have been massive disappointments to this point, so the question is whether teams view Lacy in the same tier as Robinson and Gibbs, two true superstars at the position. Based on Renner's insight, it doesn't sound like that's the case.
Whether Lacy would return to Ole Miss or look for more money and a change of scenery in the transfer portal is another question entirely, but the NFL Draft clearly isn't a foregone conclusion. That said, another season at the college level isn't a slam dunk either.We've already seen what injuries have done to Lacy's stock this fall. What if he comes back and gets injured again in 2027? Then he's probably looking at a late-round NFL Draft projection, which would be a cataclysmic fall from where his stock was entering the 2026 season. Is it worth the risk for Lacy just to move 20-30 picks up the board? At least he could get a multi-year contract at the NFL level.There is no clear path forward for Lacy, and the pre-draft process will be critical in helping him make a final decision.

        The NFL trade deadline did not exactly bring Fantasy blessings, outside of Minnesota. And we have four teams on a bye, including the Chicago Bears. So we need some positive injury news to keep us from scraping the bottom of the barrel for starting options in Week 10. So far, the results are best described as mixed and questionable. This is how we're viewing the injury report ahead of Thursday Night Football, where the Giants will get Cam Skattebo back and we'll start him as an RB2.Garrett Wilson and Omar Cooper Jr. working their way backThis is fantastic news for everyone except for Adonai Mitchel managers. Wilson progressed to a non-contact jersey on Thursday and we expect him to clear the concussion protocol in plenty of time. He's a WR2 in all formats. Cooper and Mitchell are both boom-bust WR3s. It is tough to guess which one will be ranked higher by Sunday morning, but it may come down to whether Cooper logs a full practice by Friday. Geno Smith is one of the top streaming options against the Bills, with all of his pass catchers expected to play.Xavier Worthy a surprise full practice on WednesdayWe expected Worthy to miss Week 10 but this report changed our minds. There may just be too many mouths to feed in Kansas City after the addition of Josh Downs. For now, we are projecting Rashee Rice as a WR2, Travis Kelce as a TE1, and we are waiting to see how Worthy and Downs are deployed before we start him. If you can only roster one, we would prefer Downs. But it may take him a couple of weeks to earn Patrick Mahomes' trust.David Montgomery returned to practice on Thursday, Woody Marks absentIf both guys play,  Woody Marks would lose all his appeal as an RB2 and Montgomery would be a touchdown-dependent flex. For now, we are still projecting Montgomery out and Marks in, which puts Marks around RB20 in a fantastic matchup against the Browns. But it is worth noting that Marks tweaked his knee at Wednesday's practice and missed Thursday's practice. So he could be in trouble. If both Montgomery and Marks miss Week 10, Emari Demercado is the next man up. He is worth an add in very deep leagues.
Rhamondre Stevenson and A.J. Brown both in Germany with teamIn a bit of a surprise, Stevenson was seen working on the side at Thursday's practice. It is important to note that neither of these players has been ruled out, which makes Thursday decisions a little more difficult. For now, we aren't expecting either and rank Corey Kiner as a borderline RB2 and Demario Douglas as a low-end WR2. If either returns, you probably have to start them and bench Kiner. Douglas would still be an upside WR3 even if Brown is able to go this week.George Pickens still limitedPickens missed last week with a hamstring injury after getting in multiple limited sessions and so far he is on the same path in Week 10. We aren't ranking him yet and you should have a backup plan in place. That being said, Pickens has not been ruled out yet and we are hopeful for a full practice on Friday. If Pickens is out, Ryan Flournoy is a WR3. If Pickens gets a full practice in and plays, we will rank him as a top 24 wide receiver.
Zonovan Knight looks to return from concussion protocolLike Garrett Wilson, Knight shed the non-contact jersey on Thursday. We expect him to clear the concussion protocol and rank him as the best Cardinals running back this week. This is a bad matchup and Carson Beck may not have a great debut, which is why the Cardinals have an implied total of 15. In other words, neither Knight nor Wilson are ranked as starters, but if you need a flex, we prefer Knight.

title: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh implores NFL to investigate 'loophole' that nixed Daiyan Henley trade - CBS Sports
description: The Broncos and Chargers called off their agreed-upon trade following Henley's physical
body:
The Broncos and Chargers called off their agreed-upon trade following Henley's physical
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:34 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The trade that was supposed to send Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos is off. When the Broncos announced that the deal would not be finalized, they did not disclose the reason why the agreement fell apart. But Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh pulled back the curtain and shed light on the negotiations, calling upon the NFL to look into a "loophole" that caused the trade to crumble.Although both teams announced the deal ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, both noted that it was contingent upon Henley completing a physical. It was that examination that led to the trade being called off. According to ESPN, the physical raised concerns inside the Broncos' front office about Henley's knee.Harbaugh said the Broncos used their findings to negotiate trade compensation after the deadline passed. This is permitted, as long as the teams do not add other players to the trade package. The initial deal called for the Broncos to send a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chargers in exchange for Henley."The Broncos based a pass/fail on a medical grade based on whether we would take less compensation," Harbaugh said on Thursday after the deal collapsed. "We wouldn't, and we didn't. In my opinion, it's one of those loopholes that the league should really look into, because it sets a bad precedent and continues to set a bad precedent."
Henley has only missed three games in his NFL career and just two (in 2023) due to injury. He was on the injury report in Week 6 with a knee issue but practiced in a limited fashion all three days and participated in that week's game. He appeared again on last week's injury report, but it was due to a shoulder problem rather than another knee ailment, and he practiced in full on Thursday and Friday.Harbaugh said that teams "shouldn't be" allowed to renegotiate trade terms after the deadline regardless of what does or does not come up in physical examinations."That's why it's a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that," Harbaugh said. "It's a medical grade. It's a pass/fail for a medical trade. They told us they weren't going to pass him if there was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon. They would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a 'fill in the blank.' I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is."
The picture Harbaugh painted is one where the Broncos were still open to giving up the 2027 fourth-round pick but wanted to reduce the value of the second pick. According to ESPN, Denver proposed a counteroffer of a fourth-rounder and seventh-rounder or a fourth-rounder and a pick swap. The Broncos still reportedly wanted Henley but not at the agreed-upon price."Medical grades should be based on pass/fail, what the medical grade is, not being used by an organization to get less compensation for a trade that was agreed upon," Harbaugh said.Henley was set for a team upgrade himself, as the trade would have sent him from the NFL's only winless squad to the AFC West leader. He has shined individually despite the Chargers' woes and is the team leader in tackles (51) and fumble recoveries (2) and posted two tackles for loss and an interception across his first eight games of the year. Since he joined the starting lineup in 2024, he has been a perennial 100-tackle linebacker and is on pace to cross that threshold again this season.
The Broncos' starting lineup is already set at the inside linebacker spots with Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad occupying the middle of the stout defense, so Henley would have likely arrived as a premier depth option.Henley is in the final year of his rookie contract and will be an unrestricted free agent at the end of the season.

title: Tennessee, Indiana among College Football Playoff contenders on Week 11 upset alert - CBS Sports
description: Could Saturday mark the end of the road for multiple College Football Playoff contenders?
body:
Could Saturday mark the end of the road for multiple College Football Playoff contenders?

        The second College Football Playoff rankings may have a short shelf life if Week 11 features several unexpected results among CFP contenders.Reigning national champion Indiana hosts USC in a game dripping with Big Ten title and CFP implications that should have the selection committee's attention, while elsewhere in the conference, unbeaten UCLA gets the slate started on Friday night against Illinois, which took out Oregon a few weeks ago. Then there's the SEC, where three teams in the playoff picture could do down this weekend. Another setback down the stretch for a team already trying to stabilize themselves with two losses could be fatal. With only a few weekends left to repair a résumé, here are five favorites we're nervous about backing this week.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 9 Indiana Opponent: vs. No. 18 USC (+7.5)When you play with fire, you eventually get burned -- and that could happen to the Hoosiers this weekend against a feisty Trojans team. Coming off the win over Ohio State, this is the best USC has looked all season, and the chance to control their own destiny in the CFP is the reward here. Indiana has won back-to-back games since losing to the Buckeyes, and both were in overtime. If inconsistency continues for Indiana at quarterback, USC could win this outright in Bloomington because we know what the Trojans will get from their signal-caller Jayden Maiava and a young core coming into their own.
        
            
                USC vs. Indiana: Five things to watch as Trojans, Hoosiers fight for their CFP lives
                
                    Robby Kalland                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 4 UCLAOpponent: vs. Illinois (+10.5)Staying inside the Big Ten, the Bruins are gunning for their 10th straight win this season under first-year coach Bob Chesney -- and very few are giving UCLA a shot nationally in the cluster of national title contenders. Was last week's blowout win at Minnesota in the second half not revealing enough? Are we not impressed by UCLA's defensive strengths? Illinois comes to the Rose Bowl on Friday night with a chance to post another big-time upset after catching Oregon on Oct. 24. The Fighting Illini have won four straight and would likely be ranked next week with a victory. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 8 Tennessee Opponent: at Texas A&M (+2.5)Will Tennessee's road woes linger under Josh Heupel? Many of the impact losses during his tenure as coach have come away from Neyland Stadium, and that's the worry this weekend in College Station against a team fighting for its life. The Aggies are on the verge of missing bowl eligibility altogether despite starting the campaign inside the top 10 and, after last week's 17-9 loss at South Carolina, are trying to find their rhythm offensively. Knocking the Vols off their journey within the CFP at-large picture would be the best win of the season and put Tennessee on life support ahead of next week's showdown with LSU. That's part of the drama here too -- could the Vols get caught looking ahead?
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 11 KentuckyOpponent: vs. Florida (+3.5)It seems as if everyone has jumped off Kentucky's wagon and assumes the Wildcats will lose one of their final three games this season and miss out on the program's first CFP appearance. The analytics and various playoff projections suggest Kentucky's chances are fading following its 28-point no-show at Tennessee, but Will Stein will have his team's attention this weekend. Florida comes in feeling hurt after losing at home to Oklahoma, and the Gators find themselves in quarterback disarray, unsure how to move forward with Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr. trading mistakes. Florida dominates the all-time series, but the Wildcats have won four of their last five meetings. They're hoping to make it six to stay in the discussion.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 17 South CarolinaOpponent: at Arkansas (+7.5)
This one's dangerous for the Gamecocks for three reasons -- what looms next week against top-ranked Georgia, the health of quarterback LaNorris Sellers and the fact Arkansas has improved down the stretch. All of those factors combine to form a worry spot for a team that's won four straight and has put itself in the CFP conversation, as Shane Beamer said they would at this point last fall amid a 4-8 finish. Sellers injured his ankle in last week's victory over Texas A&M and was noticeably limping in the final moments. His availability will depend on how much this offensive staff feels he's needed to beat the Razorbacks prior to what could be a season-defining matchup with Georgia. Lose Saturday night, however, and that opportunity at home looks quite different.

        While no one has officially confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino is departing the United States men's national team for Manchester United after Michael Carrick's sacking, the faces of Sebastian Berhalter and Folarin Balogun said everything that you needed to know at media availability on Thursday ahead of their Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals match with Haiti. With a spot in the Nations League final at stake in this competition, there's a need to be professional during this, and they stressed that, but it was also hard to hide emotions when the manager under whom they experienced some of their best times as USMNT internationals and an entire World Cup is about to depart.When asked about what he wanted to see, Balogun was succinct, saying, "If I had a vote, I would like to keep things the way they are."   He continued, saying, "I think things have been working well; we have a clear sense of identity, we have a clear playing style, and whenever you have a top coach, you'd want him to stay, as it's a no-brainer, so I think for us it's no different."   It's hard not to feel for Balogun after he became the story of the World Cup for the wrong reasons due to his red card being rescinded before playing against Belgium in the round of 16, where the USMNT suffered a 4-1 loss, crashing out of the tournament. Then things went from bad to worse with his move to Everton being called off due to a change in contract terms, and now needing to struggle for playing time at Monaco. While he still plans to depart the French club in January, the national team camp was supposed to be an escape, and instead, it has become another uncertain time as Pochettino's exit nears. Berhalter confirmed that the team haven't officially heard anything, but that their focus is still on the game at hand.
"We're focused on going against Haiti twice; they're a good team. You saw at the World Cup, they surprised people, so that's our main focus, and I think the group is ready to play these games," Berhalter said.   Berhalter made his national team debut under Pochettino and hasn't looked back, securing 22 caps for the team and making decisions hard on the Argentine on how he should set up the midfield. Because of that, it's hard not to be reflective during uncertain times such as this."Personally, on the field and off the field, he's done a lot for me, and from day one he's always believed in me. Before I set foot on the field, I think about the way I play and the way that I try to carry myself," Berhalter said. "He just said it doesn't matter what you're doing on the field; these are already the right things. And to be honest, I can't thank him enough, and regardless if he's coach, not the coach and, I say it every time that he's meant so much to me. And he's helped me develop as a player and as a person, and as a player, that's all you can ask for: to have that trust and have that belief in you. And for me, it's easy to go out there and just do my job so, he's meant a good deal to me for sure."   
This is all tough to manage while having games to play. Sure, players will state that they're going to be professionals, and these are people who have dealt with stress and needed to maintain that professionalism while doing it, but from a human perspective, it's a well-liked coach leaving on short notice. Even if people anticipated that Pochettino may not make it through to the 2030 World Cup and his departure is a symptom of a coach who has done well at the helm, that doesn't make it any easier on the players. If they go ahead quickly against Haiti on Saturday, they could turn the match into a celebration of what has been so great while playing for Pochettino, but going behind can have a cascading impact where doubt starts to creep in. It's something that the USMNT will need to avoid, even if the future is bright for this squad, no matter who is coaching them.Pochettino helped raise the standard, and with young players like Cavan Sullivan, Adri Mehmeti, Matias Albert, Neil Pierre and Julian Hall, the future is already here, and no one can feel complacent about their spots. These are things that the new coach can bring in, and Pochettino's leadership can set a new standard of what to look for."Yeah, I think the benefit and the blessing when you have a great coach is you know the standard," Balogun said. "I think Poch definitely raised the standard since he's been in charge. I think you guys have seen that, just the intensity of training, how we approach games, he's changed our way of thinking as players, from calling the friendlies that we have in certain camps official games, not official games. He wants us to just be of a mindset to go out there and win."   
"He's laid the foundation, and I think we, as players, have that ownership to not just do that because Poch was in charge; I think we have the ownership as players to carry that out because we know the standard," he continued. "So yeah, I think that's the benefit of having a top coach, and I'm sure you know whether he's here or not, the US will look to replace him with another top coach."   Who succeeds Pochettino will be important, but what the players have learned from his time will be invaluable, so the standard can't slip from here. As Balogun said, it's time to take ownership of their own future because while the coaches may change, the players tasked with leading this team back to the top of Concacaf are already here and understand the task at hand.How to watch Haiti vs. USMNT, oddsDate: Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time: 4:30 p.m. ETLocation: Nu Stadium -- Miami, FloridaTV: TBS | Live stream: HBO MaxOdds: Haiti +750; Draw +440; USMNT -350

UConn handled Michigan easily on the first Friday of the season. What followed was Wednesday's home game with Marquette that found the Wolverines trailing by seven in the first half under former assistant and first-year head coach Mike Boynton.Was Michigan really about to drop to 1-2?For a minute, it looked like it. This is the life almost any coach lives after he's promoted from within and replacing somebody great. If you're not also great, basically immediately, you're reminded of it very, very quickly.

title: The hits, misses and grades from some of college basketball's most intriguing teams (so far) - CBS Sports
description: The hits, misses and grades surrounding some of the fascinating teams in college basketball, including Michigan,
body:
The hits, misses and grades surrounding some of the fascinating teams in college basketball, including Michigan, Texas Tech, Marquette, Illinois, Iowa, Texas Tech and Virginia Tech.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:35 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Tuesday's Champions Classic is an incubator. It's two enormous games, and the rest of the college basketball slate fades into the background. Outside of a couple minutes of Florida-Florida State before Duke-Michigan State tipped off and Illinois-Texas Tech (at halftime of the Duke-Michigan State brawl), I didn't get a chance to watch a single second of anything else.
        
            
                Dismantling of Duke by Michigan State shows it might be time to recalibrate expectations for Blue Devils
                
                    Isaac Trotter                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Wednesday was a catch-up day to try and learn something. Five meaningful games were on the docket:Illinois-Texas TechMarquette-MichiganVirginia Tech-IowaUSC-CaliforniaMemphis-Vanderbilt. It's a tough gig, but someone has to do it. Let's dive into the hits, misses and grades.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Michigan WolverinesEarly hit: Michigan dug out of an early hole and seized control of Wednesday's 84-70 win over Marquette thanks to a new jumbo lineup, featuring 6-10 sniper Quinn Costello, 6-11 forward JP Estrella and 7-2 center Moustapha Thiam. That trio, paired with Michigan's star guard tandem of Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney, outscored Marquette by 22 points in 24 possessions. It's a very complementary group. Costello and McKenney are big-time, catch-and-shoot snipers. You have to respect Estrella and Thiam both as lob threats and on the glass. Cadeau is a wizard on the sticks who gets the ball where it needs to go. This lineup will get a lot more burn in Michigan's biggest tests. It may prove to be the easiest button Mike Boynton can press to create good shots. 
Early miss: Michigan has literally no depth right now. There is a very, very large gap between the top six players on the roster and how the operation runs when most of the second unit is on the floor. Grade, so far: B-
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Marquette Golden EaglesEarly hit: The newcomers can all play. Louisville transfer big man Sananda Fru was Marquette's biggest offseason acquisition, but he had a night to forget against Michigan due to foul trouble before anyone could even blink. Better days are ahead there. Liberty 5-in-5 transfer Colin Porter (21 points, five 3s), freshman wing Alex Egbuonu (nine points) and St. Thomas transfer Nolan Minnessale (five points, five rebounds, three steals, two assists) were the lone bright spots. Porter's a fun changeup who can get hot in a hurry from way downtown, even though he will get picked on defensively mercilessly. Minnessale is a real connector. Egbuonu is a 6-foot-7 hulking wing who can deck it and pressure the rim. All three look deserving of more minutes moving forward for Shaka Smart's club.Early miss: Something is off with sophomore point guard Nigel James Jr.; the potential Big East Player of the Year candidate shot 0-for-11 from the field against Michigan and sat on the pine for the final 10+ minutes of regulation. He has the same number of turnovers as buckets (five) this season. The best part of James' game was his ability to consistently get his shoulders past that first wave of defenders. He was an automatic paint touch. That rarely happened against Michigan. Athleticism and confidence are usually tied together. When you're confident, the athleticism pops. When you're not confident, it wanes. Marquette needs this to be a blip on the radar. It has no chance of competing in the Big East without James being James again. Smart didn't say that James was battling an injury, either.
Grade, so far: C
        
            
                Kansas' three-week trial thrashes Kentucky's five-month build in eye-opening Champions Classic performance
                
                    Isaac Trotter                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Illinois Fighting IlliniEarly hit: Quentin Coleman is infectious. He's someone you want to watch play every single day. The 6-foot-4 freshman guard had 19 points on nine shots, three offensive rebounds, four assists and two steals in front of a raucous Texas Tech crowd. Illinois' big second-half comeback came up short in the 84-78 loss, but Coleman was the star of the show. He's in the thick of pretty much everything. Who was the dude who flew out of nowhere to intercept a lob like a pterodactyl? Oh, it's Coleman.Who was the dude whose leg got rolled up and then checked himself back into the game, much to the Illinois staff's chagrin, even though he wasn't cleared to return quite yet? No. 11: Quentin Coleman.
Who is leaving the game to puke in a garbage can and then drilling ludicrous contested 3s later? Ah yes, Quentin Coleman.Coleman isn't playing mistake-free basketball, but he's one of the Big Ten's best guards already. The joy and fire he plays with is reminiscent of Kingston Flemings or Tyrese Maxey. You can't look away. Coleman looks every bit the part of a top-five pick in the 2027 NBA Draft. 
Early miss: Illinois is not a good defensive-rebounding team these days. Texas Tech ripped down 18 offensive rebounds against the Illini, including a couple on a critical possession late in the second half that led to a Donovan Atwell dagger. That's tied for the third-most offensive rebounds a Brad Underwood team has allowed in the last six-plus seasons. Texas Tech corralling 45% of its misses is something that will drive Underwood up a wall. All-American forward David Mirkovic is still out with a foot injury. He may be a vacuum-cleaner on the glass, but Illinois needs more from everyone else on the boards.
Grade, so far: B
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Texas Tech Red RaidersEarly hit: Mid-major portal evaluations. Hofstra transfer Cruz Davis and Wyoming transfer Damarion Dennis look like real hits. Davis was the big-name addition. He was a top-30ish transfer in the 2026 cycle for 247Sports, but you still have to go out and ball. Davis has done that. He's a maestro in pick-and-rolls and such a steadying force for a Texas Tech offense that needs a fulcrum while JT Toppin heals up. Davis is Texas Tech's cool, calm closer. He put Illinois away with two floaters, one with each hand, in Winning Time. He's really, really good.Dennis is the surprise, but maybe we should have seen it coming. The Wyoming transfer has a revving motor and a clean stroke from downtown. His defense isn't perfect yet, but Texas Tech needed a second-unit guard who can be a weapon off the ball. Dennis is doing just that by burying catch-and-shoot 3s and using cuts to make himself available. Texas Tech doesn't win that game without Dennis. Early miss: Even when JT Toppin comes back, I'm afraid that Texas Tech may not have quite enough in the tank defensively to win the National Championship. It's going to take grit and a whole lot of takeaways to stay alive.
Grade, so far: B+
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Virginia Tech HokiesEarly hit: The Jaylen Curry-Ben Hammond backcourt. Virginia Tech's guard tandem is ridiculously fast. Iowa has the personnel to be a problem defensively eventually, but Curry and Hammond blowtorched Iowa all night long in Tuesday's 93-88 overtime win. Virginia Tech is handing Curry a bunch of on-ball reps, and the twitchy lefty gave the Hawkeyes all sorts of problems with his paint pressure. It also allows Hammond to pivot to more off-ball reps. Virginia Tech can send him wiggling around screens, and he's a menace off pindowns because you have to respect him from all three levels. It's a good mix. Rugged forward Amani Hansberry is the heart and soul of this team, but Curry (25 points) and Hammond (32 points, four assists, zero turnovers) are the juice.Early miss: I'm not enamored with Virginia Tech's centers. Ben McCollum was licking his chops whenever Virginia Tech had a double-big lineup on the floor. Grade, so far: A-
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Iowa HawkeyesEarly hit: Cooper Koch looks poised to be one of the best role players in the country. Maybe it's disrespectful to call him a role player, but the 6-foot-8 forward is just an awesome, all-around player who is way more than just a shooter. Shooting 40% from downtown last year can draw eyeballs, but he's so much better now. Koch had 26 points, seven rebounds and two dimes in the Virginia Tech loss. With Bennett Stirtz off to the Oklahoma City Thunder, Ben McCollum needed a new iron man. Insert Koch. He literally played all 45 minutes in the overtime affair. The junior wing is turning into a complete player who can hunt mismatches in backdowns, guard multiple positions, rebound and be a weapon as a cutter, spacer or screener. Koch isn't an elite athlete, but his pacing, footwork, strength and deceleration all look much improved. He's really good.
Early miss: Experienced big man Cam Manyawu does not seem to be in McCollum's trust tree these days. Manyawu played just 15 minutes in this one. Iowa needs more from its vet.Grade, so far: B
                            
    
                                                
                    
    USC TrojansEarly hit: Rodney Rice looks healthy. A nasty shoulder injury forced him to miss all but six games last season, but the 6-foot-5 guard is back and balling. He had 32 points and nine assists in USC's win over Wichita State on Sunday, but I thought his decision-making was pretty good in Wednesday's 77-65 win over Cal. Mark Madsen is experimenting with a new aggressive, blitzing defense, so Rice was seeing double teams all game long. He did a nice job of staying in control, finding the open man and helping USC keep the advantage. He's going to have to take some tough shots in USC's iso-heavy offense, so the efficiency may suffer, but he's processing the game well. Rice had 19 points, five rebounds, three assists and just two turnovers in 39 minutes. Early miss: The rollercoaster continues for Darius and Adonis Ratliff. Darius had three fouls in five minutes. Adonis had two fouls in four minutes. The toolsy, athletic twins are still a work in progress. Some of the flashes of size, skill and length are tantalizing. Some of the shot selection and lack of force are also maddening. Eric Musselman is a former NBA coach who heavily leans into matchup-based rotations. He quickly realized both the Ratliff brothers didn't have it and wasn't afraid to yank 'em. USC's approach this year will be to let  Rice and Alijah Arenas do just about everything offensively. The three other players on the floor will be the ones who do everything else and get out of Rice and Arenas' way. Wednesday's trio was Jacob Cofie (for his defense, passing and rebounding), KJ Lewis (for his defense, secondary playmaking, cutting and dawg) and Jadis Jones (for defense and cutting). 
If you don't do that stuff, you won't play. Grade, so far: B-
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Vanderbilt CommodoresEarly hit: Vanderbilt's A-game is terrifying. Memphis is a much-improved team, but very few teams would've beaten Vanderbilt on Tuesday. Memphis had no shot at slowing down the runaway train. The Dores rolled 105-81. Hot take: Vanderbilt will go undefeated on the nights it gets six triples from its frontcourt trio of Bangot Dak, Sebastian Williams-Adams and Berke Buyuktuncel. Memphis understandably did not defend those guys like shooters, but the big fellas buoyed Vanderbilt early with triples. Then Ace Glass hit the flow state. He scored 23 points in a flash. It hit Memphis like a tsunami. Vanderbilt's a good team this year because it has much-improved size and loads of strong defenders around All-American point guard Tyler Tanner. But when they also make jumpers? Warm the bus up.Early miss: Nothing major. Vanderbilt played great. Let's check back in when it plays Ohio State in 12 days.Grade, so far: A

        Louisiana basketball's nonconference tilt against UNC-Wilmington on Saturday has been postponed "due to an insufficient number of available student-athletes," the school announced Thursday. The school mentioned that it will try to reschedule the contest.The Ragin' Cajuns only had nine players available in Monday's 56-39 win over Southern New Orleans. Tyshawn Duncan, Deion Ware and the high-flying Todd Jones are injured and have not played this season for Quannas White's club. 6-foot-8 forward Dani Pounds, who scored 15 points in the opening-night loss 75-61 against Akron, missed Monday's game with an illness. That same sickness has apparently spread through the roster, forcing Louisiana to postpone. Louisiana sits 1-2 overall this season with a 67-60 loss to Texas A&M Corpus Christi sandwiched between the Akron defeat and the win over Southern New Orleans.
This is just the second year for White at Louisiana after being one of Kelvin Sampson's top-shelf assistants at Houston for close to a decade. Louisiana went 11-22 and 7-11 in the Sun Belt last season, but a bounceback season was expected. The Ragin' Cajuns were picked sixth in the 2026-27 Sun Belt preseason poll.

title: UEFA Women's Champions League: Arsenal snap Barcelona win streak with 1-1 draw at Camp Nou - CBS Sports
description: Frida Maanum struck early and the Gunners held on for an impressive result away
body:
Frida Maanum struck early and the Gunners held on for an impressive result away

        The last time FC Barcelona lost a match in the UEFA Women's Champions League was during the 2024-25 UWCL final in Lisbon. Arsenal walked off in Lisbon, Portugal, as Champions League winners and lifted the trophy as Europe's best. On Thursday, Arsenal went into Camp Nou and walked away with a different kind of tournament upset but valuable for their momentum: a 1-1 draw against the current title holders, Barcelona. Barca's league phase win streak is snapped at three, and Arsenal's efforts lift them inside the top four for the league phase standings. Frida Maanum's goal put the Gunners on the board, while Caroline Graham Hansen equalized for Barcelona. After the final whistle, Arsenal left with the better momentum as matchday five approaches on Nov. 18. Here's how Arsenal stole the point and Barcelona leveled:  Goalkeepers turn the game on its head The visiting side took the game to Barcelona early. Immediately setting the tempo, disrupting the home side's rhythm and turning that into an early chance from Alessia Russo. The moment immediately opened the game up, and Barcelona quickly operated in the final third to record dangerous shots of their own during the opening ten minutes of the match. Arsenal's Misa Rodriguez stepped up to stop shots, made her shape bigger, and even used her face to block Barcelona's peppering of attempts on target. The team effort to shut out Barcelona in the opening half was an everybody-on-the-pitch approach, with U.S. women's national team defender Emily Fox making a goalkeeping save as well. 
"I found it hard. I mean, Barcelona is such a good team. Playing them at the Camp Nou, no, is a dream. But the match was a lot of running, a lot of defensive effort from the whole team, top to bottom, but we got the tie," Fox said after the game. "I think in the first half, their adjustment, they started to have more rotations out. So I think for us, not being stagnant and really being aggressive and trying our best to keep them out of the pockets and outside the center of the field, that was a big thing that we talked about. And then from the first half, first on corners and first on blocking shots," Fox explained. Sometimes the defensive efforts lead to transitional moments of play, and Arsenal's shift in personnel also helped change things in the game. 
 Arsenal strike first and hang on The group were motivated by the big match-up, and got on the scoreboard within the opening 25 minutes of the game. Mariona Caldentey is out with injury, and Frida Maanum's return to the lineup was an immediate game changer. Russo is the club's leading goalscorer this season; she scored a hat-trick against Benfica and is now the leading English goalscorer in the competition's history.  But her efforts against Barcelona helped set up Maanum's opening goal. It was a reminder that the Gunners do have other options even when their main outlet is in top form, and the group carried a narrow one-goal lead into halftime. 
"I think, you know, the last time we played them, we had some amazing memories, and we knew for them, coming to their place, it was going to be a hard game, and they probably saw it as a rematch, as did we," Fox said. 
"So, I think having confidence in our game plan and each other, knowing that we were going to work for each other no matter what, no matter [the] mistakes, what have you, and during halftime, we just talked about keep doing what we're doing, keep giving them a hard time, keep being aggressive, physical, bumping, and blocking them. And we have 45 minutes to go."  Barcelona still finds a way The second half was as energetic as the opening 45 minutes, and Barcelona increased the urgency even with some players unavailable due to injury. The roster flexed their depth with no Vicky Lopez, Kerolin, or Kika Nazareth, and with Aitana Bonmati only available off the bench. With her left leg wrapped in medical tape, Caroline Graham Hansen scored the equalizer just before the hour mark. 
"Happy that it's over. But yeah, I'm tired," Graham Hansen joked after the game. "No,  it was a game that I feel like we deserve to win. But on the other hand, we also have to give credit to Arsenal. Like, they were there in the last moment to block a lot of shots. Did a good job to be there with us all the way, and to try to make it difficult for us to score. But yeah, on any other given day, I think it's crazy that we don't score more goals on the chances we created today," she said. Barcelona's 24 shots and seven attempts on target essentially tripled Arsenal's shot total (seven). The other silver lining for the group, other than salvaging a point, is the efforts of their depth players to keep creating in the game. 
"I'm not surprised. I've seen them for a couple of years now, and it was just a matter of time; it was their time to step forward. It was this season, and I was very sure that it would be a matter of confidence," Graham Hansen said about her teammates stepping up. "And now, when you play more, you get more confidence, and they also take the opportunities they get and show that they're ready, they want to play, and because the quality we knew was there, so I'm not surprised, and I'm just happy for them that they are able to keep showing themselves in the big moments. Because that's what we need, and that's also what they need to keep having the confidence high for the rest of the season."
